topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the origins of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by the balance between endogenous cellular errors, inherited traits, and environmental exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how biological agents such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites drive oncogenesis, illustrated through the mechanisms and discovery of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific physical agents and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts, transversions, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental stages of host tissues facilitate the outgrowth of mutated cells.

topics.label: Methods for Determining Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and make risk-benefit assessments.
